'''Julia Laskin''' ({{langx|ru|Юлия Кимовна Ласкина}}<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Василевич |first1=Н. |last2=Шахнович |first2=И. |date=2018 |title=Услышать разговоры клеток |journal=Лаборатория и производство|language=Russian |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=8–14| url=https://labpro-media.ru/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/%D0%9B%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%BD%D0%B0.pdf }}</ref>) is the William F. and Patty J. Miller Distinguished Professor of Analytical Chemistry at [[Purdue University]]. Her research is focused on the fundamental understanding of ion-surface collisions, understanding of phenomena underlying chemical analysis of large molecules in complex heterogeneous environments, and the development of new instrumentation and methods in preparative and imaging mass spectrometry.

== Early life and education ==
Laskin was born in [[Leningrad]], Soviet Union.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Julia Laskin|language=English|oclc=4779737040}}</ref> She has said that she had a very good chemistry teacher at high school.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Focus in Honor of Dr. Julia Laskin, Recipient of the 2008 Biemann Medal|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82680999.pdf|website=Elsevier}}</ref> She studied at the [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University]], where she earned Master's of science degree in 1990.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Purdue University - Department of Chemistry - Laskin, Julia|url=https://www.chem.purdue.edu/people/profile/jlaskin.html|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.chem.purdue.edu}}</ref> When [[Perestroika]] opened the borders and allowed people to leave Russia, Laskin and her husband immigrated to Israel.<ref name=":1" /> Laskin joined the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where she worked toward a doctoral degree under the supervision of Prof. [[Chava Lifshitz]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=O’Hair|first1=Richard A. J.|last2=Siu|first2=K. W. Michael|date=2019|title=Focus in Honor of Dr. Julia Laskin, Recipient of the 2008 Biemann Medal|journal=Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry|language=en|volume=20|issue=6|pages=I1–I4|doi=10.1016/j.jasms.2009.02.023|doi-access=free|pmid=19297191 }}</ref> She earned her PhD in 1998 and moved to the [[University of Delaware]], where she worked as a postdoctoral fellow with Prof. jean Futrell.<ref name=":0" /> In 2000, Laskin joined the [[Pacific Northwest National Laboratory]] as a postdoctoral fellow.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=PNNL: Julia Laskin Received Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists|url=https://www.pnnl.gov/science/highlights/highlight.asp?id=337|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.pnnl.gov}}</ref> She was appointed a Research Scientist at the [[United States Department of Energy]] Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory in 2003 and promoted to the highest scientific rank in 2011.<ref name=":2" /> In 2017, she joined the Department of Chemistry at Purdue University as the William F. and Patty J. Miller Professor of Analytical Chemistry and was promoted to the Distinguished Professor position in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Julia Laskin, Ph.D. - Curriculum Vitae | url=https://www.chem.purdue.edu/jlaskin/documents/CV-laskin-2017.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200704214112/https://www.chem.purdue.edu/jlaskin/documents/CV-laskin-2017.pdf | archive-date=2020-07-04}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Laskin works in gas phase ion chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PNNL: Julia Laskin Honored in Prestigious Russian Journal|url=https://www.pnnl.gov/science/highlights/highlight.asp?id=576|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.pnnl.gov}}</ref> She has been involved with the development of analytical techniques to better characterize synthetic and natural polymers. She showed that the soft-landing<ref>{{Cite web|title=Purdue Chemistry: Julia Laskin Research Group: Ion Soft Landing Overview |url=https://www.chem.purdue.edu/jlaskin/research/ion/index.html|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.chem.purdue.edu|language=en}}</ref> of mass-selected ions is a powerful technique to study catalysts.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=PNNL: Julia Laskin Receives Laboratory Director's Science and Engineering Achievement Award|url=https://www.pnnl.gov/science/highlights/highlight.asp?id=3731|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.pnnl.gov}}</ref> She has also worked on the development of bioanalytical and environmental mass spectrometry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Purdue Chemistry: Julia Laskin Research Group: Research Overview|url=https://www.chem.purdue.edu/jlaskin/research/index.html|access-date=2021-09-19|website=www.chem.purdue.edu}}</ref>

Laskin served on the editorial board for the Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry (2011-2016).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Retiring JASMS Editorial Board Members |url=https://www.asms.org/publications/journal-of-the-american-society-for-mass-spectrometry-group/news-detail/2016/08/31/retiring-jasms-editorial-board-members |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=www.asms.org}}</ref> She is an editor of the ''[[International Journal of Mass Spectrometry]],''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Julia Laskin - Editorial Board - International Journal of Mass Spectrometry - Journal - Elsevier|url=http://journals.elsevier.com/international-journal-of-mass-spectrometry/editorial-board/professor-julia-laskin|access-date=2021-09-19|website=journals.elsevier.com|language=en}}</ref> and serves on the editorial advisory board for Mass Spectrometry Reviews.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mass Spectrometry Reviews Editorial Board |url=https://analyticalsciencejournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/10982787/homepage/editorialboard.html |access-date=June 5, 2022 |website=Wiley Analytical Science Mass Spectrometry Reviews|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1098-2787 }}</ref> She is Chair of the [[American Chemical Society]] Joint Board Council Committee on Publications.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Committee on Publications Roster|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/about/governance/committees/publications/roster.html|access-date=2021-09-19|website=American Chemical Society|language=en}}</ref> She was the President of the [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry]] (2022-2024), after serving as Vice President for Programs from 2020 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ASMS Board of Directors |url=https://www.asms.org/about/board-of-directors |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=www.asms.org}}</ref>

* 2017 Medal of the Russian Society for Mass Spectrometry<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tsybin|first1=Yury O.|last2=Bondarenko|first2=Pavel V.|last3=Artaev|first3=Viatcheslav B.|last4=Zubarev|first4=Roman A.|last5=Costello|first5=Catherine E.|date=2019-10-01|title=The Russian Mass Spectrometry Interest Group at ASMS: Over 20 Years of Science and Water Polo|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s13361-019-02281-9|journal=Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry|language=en|volume=30|issue=10|pages=2178–2182|doi=10.1007/s13361-019-02281-9|pmid=31392702|bibcode=2019JASMS..30.2178T|s2cid=199474674|issn=1879-1123|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* 2018 Purdue University Innovators Hall of Fame<ref>{{Cite web |title=Innovators Hall of Fame - Office of Technology Commercialization - Purdue University |url=https://www.prf.org/otc/news/innovators-hall-of-fame/index.html |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=www.prf.org}}</ref>
* 2019 [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry]] Ron Hites Award,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ron Hites Award |url=https://www.asms.org/about-asms-awards/ron-hites-award |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=www.asms.org}}</ref> along with co-authors for the article titled, Towards High-Resolution Tissue Imaging Using Nanospray Desorption Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry Coupled to Shear Force Microscopy<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nguyen |first1=Son N. |last2=Sontag |first2=Ryan L. |last3=Carson |first3=James P. |last4=Corley |first4=Richard A. |last5=Ansong |first5=Charles |last6=Laskin |first6=Julia |date=2018-02-01 |title=Towards High-Resolution Tissue Imaging Using Nanospray Desorption Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry Coupled to Shear Force Microscopy |journal=Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry |language=en |volume=29 |issue=2 |pages=316–322 |doi=10.1007/s13361-017-1750-8 |issn=1044-0305 |pmc=5787403 |pmid=28755258|bibcode=2018JASMS..29..316N }}</ref>
* 2022 Brazilian Society of Mass Spectrometry Manuel Riveros Medal<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-07-04 |title=Awards {{!}} IBERO2022 |url=https://www.ibero2022.com/registration/travelgrants_awards/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220912141306/https://www.ibero2022.com/registration/travelgrants_awards/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=September 12, 2022 |access-date=2022-12-13 |language=pt-BR}}</ref>
